metadata.title: Apple upgraded, Brinker initiated: Wall Street's top analyst calls

content.text:
The most talked about and market moving research calls around Wall Street are now in one place. Here are today's research calls that investors need to know, as compiled by The Fly.
Top 5 Upgrades:
-
HSBC upgraded Apple (AAPL) to Buy from Hold with a price target of $366, up from $260, as it believes the company is now at an "operational turning point." The "AI boost comes at the right moment, when we think Apple has one of its most innovative product pipelines in place," the firm tells investors.
-
JPMorgan upgraded 3M (MMM) to Overweight from Neutral with a price target of $180, up from $178, ahead of the Q2 report. The firm says growth is "taking hold" at 3M.
-
B. Riley upgraded AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) to Buy from Neutral with an unchanged price target of $85. Shares have declined 44% in the six months since the firm downgraded the stock, tilting "the risk/reward calculus favorably for the company."
-
Oppenheimer upgraded Ecolab (ECL) to Outperform from Perform with a $320 price target. The company's core business is performing well, driving volume and pricing growth in excess of expenses, the firm tells investors in a research note.
-
Raymond James double upgraded EchoStar (ECHO) to Strong Buy from Market Perform with a $115 price target. The firm estimates the shares are trading at a 40% discount to its sum-of-the-parts valuation.
Top 5 Downgrades:
-
Jefferies downgraded Oneok (OKE) to Hold from Buy with a price target of $95, down from $100. The firm sees a less clear growth path ahead of the company.
-
Seaport Research downgraded Sonic Automotive (SAH) to Neutral from Buy without a price target. The firm cites valuation for the downgrade with the shares up 67% year-to-date.
-
Stephens downgraded Option Care Health (OPCH) to Equal Weight from Overweight with a price target of $24, down from $30. While the firm still views Option Care as "a high-quality business" with attractive long-term industry exposure, it sees low near-term visibility into sustained earnings and limited catalysts to close the current valuation discount gap.
-
JPMorgan downgraded KKR Real Estate Finance (KREF) to Underweight from Neutral with a $6 price target ahead of quarterly results. The market is pivoting from anticipating interest rate cuts to "bracing for higher-for-longer, and potentially higher-from here," the firm says. JPMorgan also downgraded AGNC Investment (AGNC) to Neutral from Overweight with a price target of $12, up from $11.
-
Barrington downgraded Distribution Solutions (DSGR) to Market Perform from Outperform with a price target of $35, up from $33, after the company announced an agreement to be taken private for $35 per share in cash by its controlling shareholder group, LKCM Headwater.
